_what_this_is: Spending caps per issue, in US dollars, enforced by spend_ledger.check_cap before a priced run starts. A cap here is a number in a committed file rather than a sentence in a conversation, which is the difference between a cap and an intention.
_why_the_number: Recorded gate runs cost $2.56 to $10.63 each, and the first full run on a new issue is the expensive one because SOURCE searches every claim. A re-gate after corrections is roughly $2. An issue that has been through a first run, an outside review, two re-gates and a counterexample hunt should land near $25. $40 leaves room for a bad week; hitting it means something is wrong with the process, not with the budget.
_why_the_study_cap: ruled 2026-10-20, protocol rev 27. Each reliability-study issue (issue.json "study": true) has a $50 limit, set before the freeze. If an answer cannot finish within it, that is recorded as a result and the limit is not raised. The day cap below still applies, and a run picks up the next day.
_why_the_study_judging_day_cap: advisor ruling 2026-10-23: the reliability study's judge runners (judge_m1.py, judge_m2.py) check their own daily cap, summed over the judging ledger issues only, and the per-run cap; not the $25 day cap below or any WHU issue cap. The study total is still bounded by the $300 check.
_default_per_day_raise: Raised from 25 to 60 by Fred on 2026-10-30 for the WHU validity phase (validity_plan.md); back to 25 when the phase ends or at 2026-11-30T23:59Z, whichever is first; the $350 phase cap is unchanged.
_why_the_day_cap: A per-issue cap cannot see work that is not attributed to an issue -- every Signal script, the golden set, the sweeps -- nor a bad afternoon spread across three issues. This ceiling covers everything and does not depend on getting attribution right. It matters most now that jobs can run unattended.
_why_whu_check_preview: Fred's brief, 2026-10-28: the unlisted 'check an AI answer' preview (backend/routers/whu_check.py) spends on ledger issue whu-check-preview, $20 in total and $10 per UTC day, checked before each job's first model call; over means 402 and no call.
_why_whu_check_fresh_v8: Advisor ruling 2026-11-02, Fred's approval: line 'fresh-set stage 1', $60, outside the $350 WHU validity phase (validity_plan.md §12; pilot doc §16.9). The v8 run on the 18 fresh answers; judging (stage 2) needs a separate approval. Raised to $75 by advisor ruling, Fred's approval, 2026-11-04: the free prepare's likely $62.26 passed $60; the run goes ahead across days under the room rule and cost is reported as a failed bar from the measured spend.
_why_whu_check_fresh_judge: Advisor ruling 2026-11-04, Fred's approval: line 'fresh-set stage 2', $80, outside the $350 WHU validity phase (validity_plan.md §12). The two M1 judges, first reads only, on the frozen-sample sentences v8 judged BACKED or NOT BACKED; check_pilot/fresh_judge.py.
_why_whu_lean_orch_t1: Advisor ruling 2026-11-07, 'orchestrator trial 1': one paid orchestrator run on WHU-Q1-02, from the lean runs line (validity_plan.md §12; $10.05 left on it). $10, the run cap also in the issue's run_cap_usd.
_why_new_questions_line: Advisor ruling, Fred's approval, 2026-11-07: line 'new-questions test', $150, outside the $350 WHU validity phase (validity_plan.md §12). Summed over every ledger issue starting whu-cf-; the runner checks it before each paid call (built with the comparison rule, before any call).
